scores.evidence: Keyword search matters for error codes, SKUs and feature names.
scores.rationale: Hybrid RRF, cross-encoder rerank, citation ID checks and retrieval-time visibility filtering are accurate; minor slips (prompt as part of injection defense, 'prefer newest updated_at') have little design consequence.

scores.evidence: Account-specific actions like refunds, order lookups or password resets. Those need authenticated tool calls and belong in phase 2.
scores.rationale: Covers core RAG support needs with explicit exclusions, but handoff payload includes 'account context' despite no auth in v1, and there are no regional or privacy constraints.
Components and flows are consistent; minor loose ends include handoff with account context while v1 is unauthenticated, and 'two failed answers' versus 'negative feedback' triggers.

scores.evidence: Run evals in CI on any change to prompts, chunking or models.
scores.rationale: A golden set from real tickets, retrieval and faithfulness metrics, an adversarial set, CI regression and an A/B test are all present; the 85% recall threshold is unjustified and the post-launch regression monitoring is thin.

scores.evidence: I don't know your stack, doc platform, or traffic yet, so this plan uses common defaults and marks the choices that depend on your answers.
scores.rationale: Assumptions and open questions are stated clearly, but sensitivity (what changes if they're wrong) is not analyzed and numbers like 4s p95 are unjustified.

scores.evidence: Hallucinated policies (refunds, pricing) | Strict grounding, citation checks, confidence gate, escalation for policy topics
scores.rationale: Covers hallucination, staleness, injection, PII and frustration, but there's little on sync failure or partial failures, LLM or vendor outages, abuse or rate limiting, and the injection defense is thin.
Logging, a weekly review and phased rollout exist, but there is no rollback, alerting, ownership, incident response or index re-embedding migration plan.

scores.evidence: Cache frequent Q&A, use a smaller model by default, cap context size
scores.rationale: Controls are named and token cost is logged, but there is no per-conversation estimate, no scaling analysis and no build-cost discussion; extra LLM calls for rewrite, judge and synthetic questions go uncosted.

scores.evidence: record the model version on each chunk so you can re-embed later.
scores.rationale: Embedding versioning and 'pick whatever you already run' show some awareness, but there is no abstraction, exit path or discussion of the vendor and index lock-in.

scores.evidence: Generate 3–5 synthetic questions per article and index them as extra retrieval keys.
scores.rationale: Query rewrite, reranker, synthetic questions, LLM judge and model routing are all included from the start without a baseline-first gating, though each is modest.

scores.evidence: Prototype | 2 weeks | Ingestion, hybrid retrieval, basic chat, first eval set; offline retrieval recall@5 of at least 85%
scores.rationale: The phased build has concrete chunking and retrieval parameters and checkable gates, but stack choices are left open and there is no adaptation plan if results disappoint.

checklist.evidence: Run incremental syncs on article update/delete, plus a nightly full reconcile.
Split along the heading structure (H2/H3 sections), about 300–800 tokens per chunk
200–500 real questions pulled from past tickets and chat logs.
Answer only from the provided context. If the context doesn't contain the answer, say so and offer a human.
low retrieval confidence, the user asks for a human, sensitive intent, two failed answers in a row, or negative feedback.
Keep strict system-prompt boundaries and give the bot no tool access in v1.
enforce visibility filters at retrieval time, not in the prompt.
detect and redact card numbers, SSNs and passwords in user input before logging.
Account-specific actions like refunds, order lookups or password resets. Those need authenticated tool calls and belong in phase 2.
top unanswered and low-confidence questions. These are content gaps to send to the docs team
Cache frequent Q&A, use a smaller model by default, cap context size

traps.evidence: Cites the help article(s) behind every answer
Run incremental syncs on article update/delete, plus a nightly full reconcile.
Run evals in CI on any change to prompts, chunking or models.
Query rewriting: turn the latest user message plus chat history into a standalone search query.

note: A solid, grounded, eval-driven RAG plan with explicit scope and good retrieval and handoff design. Weak on privacy and retention, cost quantification, operations and rollback, and it builds a fairly rich pipeline from the start.
